June 15, 2026 
 
The Honorable Mehmet Oz, M.D. 
Administrator 
Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services 
U.S. Department of Health and Human Services 
7500 Security Boulevard 
Baltimore, MD 21244 
 
Re: CMS-0062-P â€“ Medicare and Medicaid Programs; Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act; Interoperability 
Standards and Prior Authorization for Drugs for Medicare Advantage Organizations, Medicaid Managed Care 
Plans, State Medicaid Agencies, Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP) Agencies and CHIP Managed Care 
Entities, and Issuers of Qualified Health Plans on the Federally-Facilitated Exchanges 
 
Submitted electronically via regulations.gov 
 
 
Dear Administrator Oz: 
 
The Health Innovation Alliance (HIA) appreciates the opportunity to comment on CMS-0062-P. HIA is a diverse 
coalition of patient advocates, health care providers, consumer organizations, employers, technology companies, 
and payers who support the commonsense use of data and technology to improve health outcomes and lower costs. 
 
HIA strongly supports CMS's continued efforts to modernize prior authorization through interoperable, standards-
based technologies. Prior authorization remains a significant source of administrative burden for patients, providers, 
and health plans. Electronic prior authorization can help reduce delays in care, improve transparency, and support 
more timely access to medically appropriate therapies. 
 
As CMS advances electronic prior authorization, HIA believes three principles are particularly important: 
â€¢ 
providers should have access to actionable coverage and prior authorization information at the point of 
care to support informed treatment decisions and reduce avoidable delays;  
â€¢ 
electronic prior authorization solutions should be integrated into existing clinical and prescribing 
workflows to maximize adoption and minimize burden; and  
â€¢ 
CMS should continue leveraging nationally recognized interoperability standards and implementation 
approaches that have achieved meaningful adoption across the healthcare ecosystem. 
 
HIA appreciates CMS's efforts to advance these goals through the proposals included in CMS-0062-P and offers 
the following comments. 
 
Point-of-Care Transparency and Coverage Information 
HIA has consistently supported policies that make actionable coverage and utilization management information 
available at the point of care. Greater transparency regarding coverage requirements can help providers make more 
informed treatment decisions, reduce administrative burden, and improve patients' ability to access appropriate 
therapies. 
 
Providers should have access, within existing clinical workflows whenever possible, to information regarding prior 
authorization requirements; coverage limitations and utilization management policies; step therapy requirements; 
 
 
2
formulary status; alternative covered therapies; and documentation requirements needed to support coverage 
determinations. 
 
Providing this information at the point of prescribing can help reduce unnecessary prior authorization requests, 
minimize treatment delays, and improve the efficiency of care delivery. Further, embedding standards like F&B 
and RTPB data into EHR and e-prescribing workflows can help prescribers choose the best option for the patient, 
likely shortening treatment initiation timelines, and improving patient adherence. 
 
In addition, HIA supports efforts that provide clinicians with greater visibility into coverage, formulary, and benefit 
information before a prior authorization request is initiated. Access to actionable coverage information within 
prescribing workflows can help providers identify appropriate therapeutic options, avoid unnecessary 
administrative processes, and support more timely initiation of treatment. 
 
CMS's continued efforts to improve the availability and usability of this information are an important component of 
broader interoperability and administrative simplification initiatives. 
 
Expanding Electronic Prior Authorization for Drugs  
HIA supports CMS's proposal to expand the Prior Authorization API framework established in the CMS 
Interoperability and Prior Authorization final rule (CMS-0057-F) to support drugs covered under the medical 
benefit. 
 
Prescription drug therapies paid under the medical benefit are often clinically significant and time-sensitive 
components of a patient's care plan. Delays associated with manual prior authorization processes can contribute to 
treatment interruptions and administrative burden for both providers and patients. 
 
Extending existing Prior Authorization API capabilities to drugs covered under the medical benefit will help 
promote a more consistent and streamlined prior authorization experience across covered items, services, and 
therapies. HIA agrees that leveraging the existing standards-based framework established through prior CMS 
interoperability efforts can facilitate more efficient information exchange, support electronic documentation 
submission, and improve the timeliness of coverage determinations. 
 
Accordingly, HIA supports CMS's proposal to incorporate drugs covered under the medical benefit into the existing 
Prior Authorization API framework. HIA also supports CMS's proposal to extend electronic prior authorization 
requirements for drugs covered under the pharmacy benefit across additional federal healthcare programs. 
 
A consistent approach to pharmacy-benefit prior authorization can help reduce administrative burden on providers, 
simplify implementation for health IT developers and plans, and improve the efficiency of prescribing workflows. 
Greater alignment across programs can also reduce variability in how prior authorization requests are initiated and 
processed, helping clinicians navigate coverage requirements more effectively. 
 
Recognizing Electronic Prior Authorization Standards 
HIA agrees with CMS's approach of building upon standards and implementation approaches that have already 
achieved meaningful adoption within the healthcare ecosystem. Leveraging existing investments can reduce 
implementation complexity while accelerating the benefits of electronic prior authorization for patients and 
providers. 
 
We agree that naming two sets of standards to be used, one (FHIR Da Vinci) for drugs paid for under the medical 
benefit and one (NCPDP SCRIPT, F&B, and RTPB) for drugs paid for under the prescription benefit both 
establishes continuity with previous federal law and regulations (eg. 2024 Interoperability and Prior Authorization 
final rule and rules implementing ePA for drugs in Medicare Part D and MA-PDs) and is congruent with the intent, 
capabilities, and adoption of both sets. 
 
 
3
 
The Alliance also commends CMS's proposal to require not only NCPDP SCRIPT but also the F&B and RTPB 
standards. These two standards work upstream of the prior authorization transaction itself, enabling prescribers to 
make better-informed therapy choices before a PA request is ever initiated. A significant share of prior 
authorization requests result from prescribers having no real-time visibility into payer coverage rules at the time of 
prescribing.  
 
Implementation Considerations 
HIA appreciates CMS's recognition that successful implementation requires balancing urgency with operational 
readiness. 
 
We support timely implementation of these policies, understanding that adequate lead time, clear implementation 
guidance, and coordination with industry stakeholders will be important to achieving the full benefits of electronic 
prior authorization while minimizing disruption. 
 
CMS should continue to promote consistent implementation approaches, reduce unnecessary complexity wherever 
possible, and support adoption across organizations of varying size and technical capability. 
 
Response to CMS Request for Information: Cybersecurity and Trust Frameworks 
HIA appreciates CMS's recognition that interoperability and cybersecurity must advance together. As healthcare 
increasingly relies on digital infrastructure and API-enabled information exchange, maintaining the security, 
integrity, and availability of health information systems is essential.  
 
HIA encourages CMS to continue coordinating closely with the Office of the National Coordinator for Health 
Information Technology (ONC), the HHS Office for Civil Rights (OCR), and other federal partners to promote 
consistent and complementary cybersecurity expectations across federal programs. 
 
HIA supports risk-based cybersecurity approaches that preserve secure exchange of health information while 
avoiding unnecessary barriers to interoperability and innovation. CMS should continue to leverage widely adopted 
industry standards, frameworks, and best practices, while minimizing duplicative compliance and reporting 
requirements whenever possible. 
 
As interoperability requirements continue to evolve, alignment across federal agencies will help reduce complexity 
for healthcare organizations and technology developers while strengthening the security of health information 
exchange. 
 
Conclusion 
HIA appreciates CMS's commitment to advancing interoperability, reducing administrative burden, and improving 
patient access to care through standards-based electronic prior authorization processes. 
 
We support CMS's efforts to modernize prior authorization through approaches that improve transparency, integrate 
into existing clinical workflows, and build upon established interoperability standards and industry investments. We 
believe these proposals represent an important step toward a more efficient, patient-centered healthcare system and 
encourage CMS to finalize these provisions. 
 
We appreciate the opportunity to provide comments and look forward to continued engagement with CMS on these 
important issues. 
 
Sincerely, 
 
 
4
 
Roslyn Docktor 
Executive Director 
Health Innovation Alliance

# Comment Analysis Template: CMS-2026-1255-0001

## 1. COMMENTER INFORMATION

- **Author/Organization name:** Health Innovation Alliance (HIA); signed by Roslyn Docktor, Executive Director
- **Stakeholder type:** Advocacy Group / Multi-stakeholder coalition
- **Credentials or expertise mentioned:** Coalition of patient advocates, health care providers, consumer organizations, employers, technology companies, and payers focused on data and technology to improve outcomes and lower costs.

## 2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

HIA strongly supports CMS's proposal to modernize prior authorization for drugs using interoperable, standards-based technologies. The comment endorses point-of-care transparency, expansion of the Prior Authorization API to medical benefit drugs, use of NCPDP standards for pharmacy benefit drugs, and cybersecurity coordination that avoids duplicative requirements.

## 3. REGULATORY CONTEXT

- **Specific provisions addressed:** PA-DRUG-MEDICAL; PA-DRUG-PHARMACY; FHIR-IG-REQUIRED; PA-DENIAL-REASONS; PA-TIMEFRAMES-DRUGS; STAKEHOLDER-COORDINATION/GENERAL RFI on cybersecurity and trust frameworks.
- **Regulatory citations mentioned:** No CFR sections cited directly. The comment references CMS-0062-P, CMS-0057-F, the 2024 Interoperability and Prior Authorization final rule, and Medicare Part D/MA-PD ePA rules.
- **Standards referenced:** FHIR Da Vinci; NCPDP SCRIPT; Formulary and Benefit (F&B); Real-Time Prescription Benefit (RTPB); nationally recognized interoperability standards.

## 4. DETAILED POSITIONS

**Topic 1: Point-of-Care Coverage Transparency**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL; PA-DRUG-PHARMACY
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** Actionable coverage, formulary, utilization management, step therapy, alternative therapy, and documentation information in clinical and prescribing workflows can reduce avoidable PA requests and treatment delays.
- **Specific request:** CMS should continue improving the availability and usability of coverage information at the point of care and support embedding F&B and RTPB data in EHR/e-prescribing workflows.

**Topic 2: Medical Benefit Drug Prior Authorization API**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DRUG-MEDICAL; FHIR-IG-REQUIRED
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** Medical benefit drugs are often clinically significant and time-sensitive, and manual PA processes contribute to interruptions and burden.
- **Specific request:** Finalize the proposal to incorporate medical benefit drugs into the existing Prior Authorization API framework.

**Topic 3: Pharmacy Benefit Drug ePA Standards**
- **Provision ID:** PA-DRUG-PHARMACY
- **Position:** Support
- **Rationale:** A consistent approach using NCPDP SCRIPT, F&B, and RTPB can simplify implementation for providers, plans, and developers and align with existing federal rules and adoption patterns.
- **Specific request:** Finalize electronic prior authorization requirements for pharmacy benefit drugs across additional federal healthcare programs.

**Topic 4: Implementation and Cybersecurity Coordination**
- **Provision ID:** GENERAL
- **Position:** Modify / Clarify
- **Rationale:** Implementation should balance urgency with operational readiness, while cybersecurity expectations should be risk-based, coordinated, and non-duplicative.
- **Specific request:** Provide clear guidance, stakeholder coordination, consistent implementation approaches, and coordination with ONC, OCR, and other federal partners.

## 5. SOLICITATION RESPONSES

- **S12:** Supports expanding the FHIR-based Prior Authorization API to medical benefit drugs and notes that existing standards-based capabilities can improve documentation exchange and timeliness.
- **S14:** Supports applying pharmacy benefit ePA requirements across additional federal programs using NCPDP standards.
- **S21:** Supports timely implementation but emphasizes adequate lead time, guidance, and coordination.
- **S22:** Suggests that using adopted NCPDP standards and existing investments can reduce implementation complexity.
- **S25:** Supports requiring F&B and RTPB because they provide upstream coverage visibility before a PA request is initiated.
- **S28:** Supports alignment with existing Part D and MA-PD ePA rules and standards.
- **S66-S82:** Responds generally to RFI themes on cybersecurity/trust frameworks by recommending risk-based, coordinated federal expectations.

## 6. RECOMMENDATIONS

1. Finalize expansion of the Prior Authorization API to medical benefit drugs.
2. Finalize pharmacy benefit ePA requirements using NCPDP SCRIPT, F&B, and RTPB.
3. Ensure point-of-care coverage and utilization management information is available in existing clinical and prescribing workflows.
4. Provide adequate lead time, clear implementation guidance, and stakeholder coordination.
5. Coordinate cybersecurity expectations across CMS, ONC, OCR, and other federal partners while minimizing duplicative requirements.

## 7. CONCERNS & OBJECTIONS

- **Primary concerns:** Administrative burden, treatment delays, inconsistent workflows, and potential duplicative cybersecurity/compliance requirements.
- **Potential negative impacts cited:** Manual PA processes can delay therapy initiation, interrupt treatment, and burden providers and patients.
- **Implementation barriers mentioned:** Need for adequate lead time, clear guidance, coordination, consistent implementation, and support for organizations of varying size and technical capability.

## 8. SUPPORTING EVIDENCE

- **Data or statistics cited:** None.
- **Studies or research referenced:** None.
- **Examples provided:** Examples include point-of-care visibility into prior authorization requirements, coverage limitations, step therapy, formulary status, alternative covered therapies, and documentation requirements.

## 9. IMPACT ASSESSMENT

- **Affected stakeholders:** Patients, providers, payers, health IT developers, plans, and federal agencies.
- **Economic implications:** The comment implies reduced administrative costs and implementation complexity by leveraging existing standards and investments.
- **Technical feasibility:** Favorable if CMS builds on adopted standards, provides guidance, and coordinates with stakeholders.
- **Patient care impact:** Expected improvements include faster therapy initiation, fewer delays, better adherence, and more patient-centered care.

## 10. SENTIMENT ANALYSIS

- **Overall position:** Supportive
- **Tone:** Professional and collaborative
- **Priority level:** High

## 11. KEY QUOTES

1. "HIA strongly supports CMS's continued efforts to modernize prior authorization through interoperable, standards-based technologies." - Context: Overall position on the proposed rule.
2. "Providers should have access, within existing clinical workflows whenever possible, to information regarding prior authorization requirements." - Context: Point-of-care transparency recommendation.
3. "HIA supports CMS's proposal to expand the Prior Authorization API framework... to support drugs covered under the medical benefit." - Context: Support for PA-DRUG-MEDICAL.
4. "HIA supports risk-based cybersecurity approaches that preserve secure exchange of health information while avoiding unnecessary barriers." - Context: Cybersecurity and trust framework RFI response.

## 12. THEMES

- [x] **IMPLEMENTATION-TIMELINE** - HIA supports timely implementation but calls for adequate lead time, clear guidance, and stakeholder coordination.
- [x] **COST-RESOURCES** - The comment emphasizes leveraging existing investments and reducing implementation complexity.
- [x] **PROVIDER-BURDEN** - HIA repeatedly frames ePA and point-of-care transparency as ways to reduce administrative burden.
- [x] **PRIVACY-SECURITY** - The cybersecurity RFI section recommends coordinated, risk-based protections.
- [x] **TECHNICAL-FEASIBILITY** - HIA supports standards already adopted in the ecosystem and asks CMS to reduce unnecessary complexity.
- [x] **STANDARDS-MATURITY** - The comment supports FHIR Da Vinci and NCPDP standards because they align with existing rules and adoption.
- [x] **PATIENT-ACCESS** - HIA argues ePA can reduce treatment delays and improve timely access to medically appropriate therapies.
- [x] **STAKEHOLDER-COORDINATION** - The comment calls for industry coordination and federal alignment across CMS, ONC, OCR, and other partners.
- [x] **EXISTING-WORKFLOWS** - HIA asks that ePA and coverage transparency be embedded in clinical, prescribing, EHR, and e-prescribing workflows.
- [x] **VENDOR-ECOSYSTEM** - The comment notes that consistency can simplify implementation for health IT developers.
